newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures paused for breath after Monday's rally, struggling to push beyond an area of resistance at 130.40 despite another opinion poll suggesting the centre-right would win the current parliamentary election.

Both June bond and interest rate futures received a small boost at the open on the back of buying by non-residents then the bond contract hit its peak for the day after U.S. April sales fell by 0.3 percent, broadly in line with expectations.
Traders said domestic investors were the main sellers at the highs and that the contract was looking oversold on a technical basis above 130.40.
One trader, however, said that in contrast to the calm cash market of recent days there had been buying of 30-year strips by domestic investors.
June PIBOR continued to outperform Euromarks, helped partly by the strength of the French franc, narrowing the spread between the two June contracts to 29 basis points from over 40 a week ago.

Traders said short covering helped the contract initially but the gains were capped above 96.50 by others taking profits. June PIBOR has climbed more than 20 basis points during the past three sessions.
Analysts said the main risk at the moment was a swing to the left in the polls as there was a growing belief the centre-right would win and the market was positioned for such an outcome.

One trader said there was some concern when Rene Monory, a conservative politician and speaker of the French upper house, broke a political taboo in a sensitive election period by saying France's minimum wage was destined to disappear.
Late in the session a stronger-than-expected rise in the Atlanta Fed business activity index in April also weighed on the bond future.
The French franc climbed to 3.3681 against the mark, its highest level since April 18, the day after rumours a snap election would be called first hit French financial markets.
The Treasury said it would be selling 20 to 22 billion francs of two- and five-year benchmark BTANs at auction on Thursday.
